nodes.name: K3[Cr(C2O4)3]·3H2O synthesis
nodes.procedure: 1 g of potassium oxalate monohydrate and 7 g of oxalic acid dihydrate were dissolved in 100 mL of deionized water. Then, 2.5 g of powdered potassium dichromate was added carefully with vigorous stirring. When the reaction was ended, the solution was evaporated nearly to dryness and then freezing crystallized. The obtained crystal was washed with acetone three times and finally dried at 60 °C.

nodes.name: NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Solution A containing NiCl2·6H2O (0.015 mol) and FeCl3·6H2O (0.005 mol) dissolved in 50 mL of deionized water. Solution B containing K3[Cr(C2O4)3]·3H2O (0.004 mol) and (NH4)2CO3 (0.036 mol) dissolved in 40 mL of deionized water. Solution A and B were mixed and stirred vigorously. The homogenous slurry was transferred to stainless steel Teflon-lined autoclave and heated at 100 °C for 20 h. Then cooled to room temperature naturally, resulting precipitate washed several times with deionized water and dried at 60 °C.

nodes.source_text: All the electrochemical measurements were performed on CHI 600E electrochemical workstation using a typical three-electrode system at 298 K. A graphite rod was used as the counter electrode and saturated calomel electrode (SCE) as the reference electrode, while electrocatalyst was dropped on a glassy carbon electrode 5 mm in diameter, 0.196 cm^2 with the loading of 0.204 mg cm^-2 was used as the working electrode. All the linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves were recorded at a scan rate of 5 mV s^-1 with correction by eliminating iR drop in 1.0 M KOH. The NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]^3--LDHs required a low overpotential of 236 mV to reach the current density of 10 mA cm^-2 while the NiFe LDHs needed an overpotential of 272 mV. The Tafel slope of NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]^3--LDHs is 59.7 mV per decade... negligible activity degradation after 2000 CV cycles... chronopotentiometry measurement... negligible performance decay even after more than 138 h... NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]^3--LDHs exhibits higher TOF for OER at an overpotential of 270 mV (30×10^-3 s^-1)... The C_dl of NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]^3--LDHs is about 1.5 times as large as the C_dl of NiFe LDHs.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDHs shows (003) and (006) reflections at 11.4° and 23.0°. NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs shows shifted (003) and (006) peaks at 8.8° and 17.7° with interlayer distance increased to 10.02 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD results confirmed that ... K3[Cr(C2O4)3]⋅3H2O precursor, NiFe LDHs and NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs were successfully synthesized. For NiFe LDHs, the diffraction peaks located at 11.4° and 23.0° ... For NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs, two prominent low-angle reflections at 8.8° and 17.7° of (003) and (006) planes shift to lower angel, confirming the interlayer distance ... is increased from 7.75 to 10.02 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs shows Cr-O stretching at 812 cm⁻¹ and CO symmetric vibrations at ~1390 and 1265 cm⁻¹ confirming intercalation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The band located at 812 cm⁻¹ is identified as the stretching vibration of Cr-O ... For K3[Cr(C2O4)3]⋅3H2O, two peaks are observed at 1390 and 1265 cm⁻¹ which can be assigned as CO symmetric vibration modes of oxalate ... For NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs, the peak position of CO symmetric vibration changes slightly due to the interaction between intercalated [Cr(C2O4)3]3- and hydroxide layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDHs shows sheet-like morphology with lateral size 20-80 nm in hexagonal shape. NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs retains flake-like structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Typically, NiFe LDHs show sheet-like morphology with a lateral size of around 20-80 nm in a hexagonal shape (Fig. 1c). After the intercalation of [Cr(C2O4)3]3-, NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs still reserve the flake-like structure (Fig. 1d and Fig. S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDHs lattice fringe 0.26 nm (012) plane. NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs lattice fringe 0.2 nm (018) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For high-resolution TEM (HRTEM), the lattice fringe spacing of NiFe LDHs and NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs is 0.26 and 0.2 nm, respectively (Fig. 1c and d inset patterns), which corresponds to (012) and (018) planes characteristic of NiFe LDHs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, Cr, C, O elements in NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy mapping images confirm the uniform distribution of elements Ni, Fe, Cr, C, and O in NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs (Fig. 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDHs: Ni 2p3/2 indicates Ni³⁺ 24.0%, Fe 2p at 712.5 eV (3/2) and 725.4 eV (1/2) for Fe³⁺. NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]³⁻-LDHs: Ni 2p3/2 shift to higher energy with Ni³⁺ 51.2%, Fe 2p negative shift showing Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺, Cr 2p positive shift, C 1s O-C-O at 288.7 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As clearly displayed in Fig. 2(a), an apparent shift to a higher energy direction of Ni 2p3/2 peaks illustrates that NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]³⁻-LDHs have a higher proportion of Ni³⁺ species (51.2%) compared with NiFe LDHs (24.0%) ... The Fe 2p3/2 peaks located at 712.5 and Fe 2p1/2 at 725.4 eV correspond to Fe³⁺ in NiFe LDHs ... For NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]³⁻-LDHs, the negative shift in Fe 2p ... In the C 1s spectrum of NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]³⁻-LDHs (Fig. S3b), a distinct peak at 288.7 eV is attributed to O-C-O band.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge adsorption edge shifts to higher energy and Fe K-edge to lower energy in NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]³⁻-LDHs vs NiFe LDHs, confirming higher Ni valence and lower Fe valence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni K-edge XANES spectra are shown in Fig. 2(c), slightly shifting to higher energy of the adsorption edge demonstrating the increase of Ni valence state after intercalation, which is consistent with the XPS results. The Fe K-edge XANES spectra of Fig. 2(d) show that the adsorption edge slightly shifted to lower energy.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs shows decreased Ni-Ni/Fe and Fe-Ni coordination intensity indicating metal vacancies and increased structural disorder.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the intercalation of [Cr(C2O4)3]3-, an apparent decrease in intensity of the Ni-Ni/Fe coordination could be observed ... Similarly ... obvious decrease in intensity of both Fe-O and Fe-Ni coordination, suggesting the formation of metal and oxygen vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge shows continuous positive shift during OER; NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs maintains higher average Ni valence than NiFe LDHs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Ni K-edge XAS spectra indicated that the oxidation of Ni²⁺ was more inclined to occur in [Cr(C2O4)3]3- intercalated NiFe LDHs.

nodes.characterization_summary: After OER at 1.55 V, Ni³⁺ proportion increases to 47.4% (NiFe LDHs) and 77.6% (NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs).
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the OER catalytic process, the Ni³⁺ proportion of NiFe LDHs and NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs was increased to 47.4% and 77.6%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs shows strong Ni³⁺-O bands at 478 cm⁻¹ and 554 cm⁻¹ at ≥1.40 V indicating γ-NiOOH formation; NiFe LDHs shows weaker signals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Two distinct and intense bands located at 478 cm⁻¹ (bending mode of Ni³⁺-O) and 554 cm⁻¹ (stretching mode of Ni³⁺-O) are observed at 1.40 V and above for NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs ... As for NiFe LDHs, a rather weak signal intensity of two Raman peaks is exhibited.
The Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area of NiFe LDHs and NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]3--LDHs were estimated to be 76.38 m² g⁻¹ and 48.49 m² g⁻¹, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-[Cr(C2O4)3]³⁻-LDHs shows Ni²⁺ oxidation peak at ~1.38 V (vs NiFe LDHs at 1.41 V) with higher intensity, indicating lower formation energy and more Ni³⁺ sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak appeared approximately at 1.38 V can be ascribed to the oxidation of Ni²⁺ sites. Whereas in NiFe LDHs, the oxidation peak of Ni²⁺ occurred at around 1.41 V, revealing the intercalation of [Cr(C2O4)3]³⁻ reduced the formation energy from Ni²⁺ to Ni³⁺.
